scope: Static data-flow evidence for the successful merged HDR still-image branch on Q7 v1.01.
coordinates: Word locations are decoded segment offsets. E03 word locations use original firmware file offsets.
jpeg_input_transform: T(B) = B & 0x7fffffff if B & 0x40000000 is nonzero, else B | 0x20000000.

evidence.observation: HdrImageMixing allocates the block buffer descriptor at W+0x70, where W is its sp+0x20. HdrAllocBlockBufTag stores the allocated address B in descriptor word 0. HdrImageMixing saves B across PerformImageMixSubImages and publishes the saved value to HDR context+0x3dc on success.

PerformImageMixSubImages uses W+0x70 as the output subimage cursor. It copies that cursor into word 0 of its output descriptor sp+0x138. For W+0x208 equal to zero it passes that descriptor to IpuToneMapRgb with format 0xf01. Two adjacent tone-map call sites also take sp+0x138 as the output descriptor. Cursor stores can advance to further views of the allocation. IpuToneMapRgb creates a type-0 path and passes the current output address in a2 to PathSetBuffers, which stores it at path+0x28, before PathSubmit, PathGo and PathWait.

On the IpuSubmit branch with path+0x964 equal to zero, path+0x28 supplies the output descriptor surface. For the general format arm this enters ImageDescriptorCreateFromBlockBuffer and for type 7 it enters ImageDescriptorAddSurface. IpuSubmit passes the resulting descriptor as image kind 2 to CImageProcessor::SetImage. A nonzero path+0x964 selects a descriptor copied from path+0x8fc instead.

IpuToneMapRgb creates ID 0xf with version 0xc, fills signed halfwords at +0x14 through +0x24 in the newly created object, and sets then enables ID 0xf before submitting this path. The following halfwords at +0x26 and +0x28 both contain 0x800.

HdrRun calls HdrImageMixing and copies the HDR context block descriptor beginning at +0x3dc into its caller-provided output. Its caller passes sp+0x28, checks successful completion, and supplies the same descriptor with a2 equal to zero to StillCaptureHdrImageSave. StillCaptureHdrImageSave copies its image address to word 0 of its local descriptor D at sp+0x28.

StillCaptureHdrImageSave invokes StillCaptureSaveIcaCreateThumbnail. That helper supplies D as both the source and destination of StillCaptureLDCPass and sets its copy-back flag. The type-8 create parameters carry D[0] in both input and output positions at +0x18 and +0x34. The copy-back arm reads and writes through the same D pointer. The later PoolReallocEx result is not assigned into D.

The no-preexisting-code arm passes D to StillCaptureSaveCompressImage. It places D[0] in the direct compressor input parameter at +0x8 and +0xc. ApsJpegDirectCompress reads +0x8 as B, derives T(B), and writes it to its JPEG create parameter P+0x8. P+0x24 independently receives the encoded-output buffer address. PathCreate(1,P) then starts the type-1 path, and PathGetCodeSize returns encoded size through the caller-provided pointer.

JpegPathInit binds the type-1 create callback 0x801df114. PathCreateInPlace dispatches through its selected record+0x4c. The create callback reads P[0] into path+0xb8 and on its ordinary encode branch sets the destination of the first copied surface descriptor to path+0x8. It copies P+0x8 there.

The HDR preexisting-code caller supplies an image descriptor with word 0 zero. The other two observed HDR callers receive the result of StillCaptureSaveCompressImage, which writes its source descriptor address into result word 0 and clears the referenced descriptor word 0 after direct compression. StillCaptureSaveJpegImage forwards the result to ApsExifCreateJpeg. On the main descriptor check, a zero in the referenced word 0 takes the branch that uses the existing code size.

trace_limitations: Extents end at the next distinct sidecar address, not a typed ELF function size.
Linear MIPS32 word scan; edges are instruction candidates, not proof of reachability.
Delay slots are included in extents. Register-indirect targets are unresolved.
A jump is recorded as a transfer, not automatically a function call.
limitations: The address chain is static and bounded to the inspected successful HDR branch. It identifies an allocation and its subimage views through software descriptors. Physical aliases, DMA, register state and camera pixel output were not measured.
Optional HDR manipulation, photo-frame and LDC processing can change pixels while the address chain is retained. The proof concerns the descriptor path, not pixel equality.
The descriptor demonstrates a local ID 0xf submission. It does not establish that every output mode uses this matrix or rule out downstream configuration overrides.
The observed EXIF branch classification concerns the main JPEG descriptor check. Auxiliary images and other flags have separate paths.
